title: Kunza language - Wikipedia
text: Kunza (Kunza: Likanantaí) is the extinct language isolate of the Atacama people, once spoken in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile and southern Peru who have since shifted to Spanish. The last speakers were documented in 1964; however, there is currently a revitalization effort. [2] Other names and spellings include Cunza, Ckunsa, Likanantaí, Lipe, Ulipe, and Atacameño. title: Language isolate - Wikipedia
text: A language isolate, sometimes called an isolated language, is a language that has no demonstrable genealogical relationship with any other language. [1][2] That is, an isolate is a language family that only contains one member.

Cunza, also known as Likanantaí, Lipe, Ulipe, or Atacameño, is an extinct language isolate once spoken in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile and southern Perú (specifically in Peine, Socaire (Salar de Atacama), and Caspana) by the Lickan-antay people, who have since shifted to Spanish.
